identity.trade: Carts and wheels: the wheelwrights and carters of the north-west, where every wagon on the vale's roads was mended at least once.

greeting: Tithe day is never early and always too soon.
Dunhallow is a small place with a long memory. State your name slowly.
rumour: Everyone owes everyone a little. Nobody agrees on the sum.
A guild inspector came last month and left a list. We are still decoding it.
A wheel lasts four hundred miles on stone road and forty on none.

opinions.idony_farrow: Idony lives next door and hears everything I do.

time.morning: Morning. The shop is open if you are.

dialogue.aside: Argh! Oh, it is you. Sorry. The kettle and I had words. Sit.

greeting: Rooms are clean. The beds are honest about their age.
Mind the workshop. Everything here is half finished and fully dangerous.
rumour: Half my regulars have coloured hands. The mugs gave up showing it.
A man paid for a room and asked which way the stones face. I put him by the stairs.
Wood is up, iron is up, and the market will not pay more. Craft is a squeeze.
If trade slows, Dunhallow feels it first. If it speeds up, Dunhallow feels it last.

opinions.colm_hallam: Colm undercuts me. I forgive Colm. Mostly.
opinions.elfrida_shuttle: Elfrida keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.evening: Closing up. Come back tomorrow and bring coin.

dialogue.aside: Friend. Gently, now. Sit. I will make something warm.

greeting: Mind the anvil. It has opinions.
Dunhallow is wheelwrights and carters. Nobody thinks to say it, but it is true.
rumour: Hooks, needles, hasps. A craftsman wants a small tool made well.
Plough blades sell slow and spear heads sell fast. I do not like what that says.
Somebody is copying our patterns and selling them downriver. Cheaper, and worse.

opinions.idony_farrow: Idony undercuts me. I forgive Idony. Mostly.

time.night: Lamps are lit. Craft does not end at dusk, only the pay does.

dialogue.aside: Walk with me? I cannot stay still, and you are good company on the move.

greeting: Everything has a price. Some of it is even written down.
Folk come to Dunhallow for wheelwrights and carters. Some stay for the quiet.
rumour: Needles, thread, pins. I sell small things to people who make large ones.
Folk buy more than they need, then bring half back. Fear shops strangely.
Apprentices are fewer every year. The ones who stay learn fast and leave faster.
Ask anyone in Dunhallow about the Dunhallow Wagon Yard. You will get four stories and one fact.

opinions.una_chandler: I would trust Una with a purse. A small one.

time.rain: Rain on the roof. Good for the colour, bad for the drying.

greeting: Come closer. My ears are old and your voice is young.
Strangers in Dunhallow get one warning and one welcome. You are on the welcome.
rumour: Winters were colder, summers longer, and the wolves stayed home. Or so I choose to remember.
Prices at the market are off. Our work is the same. Our wages are not.
A wagon-train lost a wheel near the old beacon and the carters came home without a driver.

opinions.fenn_tilley: I would trust Fenn with a purse. A small one.

time.morning: Morning. The shop is open if you are.

dialogue.aside: Ah. You. I would say nice day, but it is not, and you would know.

greeting: Oak for the rim, elm for the hub, ash for the spokes. Argue and I will explain.
Welcome to Dunhallow. Mind the Dunhallow Wagon Yard. Everyone does, eventually.
rumour: Everyone wants iron tyres now. Iron is dear. Oak is patient.
The big order came with a seal nobody recognised. The pay was real. We did not ask.

opinions.darby_sumner: Darby knows the trade. I will say that for Darby.
opinions.una_chandler: Una works hard and talks harder.

time.evening: Closing up. Come back tomorrow and bring coin.

dialogue.aside: I dreamed of you last night. You were a heron. It suited you.

greeting: Road is mud, axle is mud, I am mud. Hello.
The Dunhallow Wagon Yard is not much to look at. It is, however, ours.
rumour: Toll keepers keep changing. Their prices are the only thing that stays the same.
Someone keeps leaving unfinished work on our benches overnight. It is always very good work.
Dunhallow fixed a Solkar wagon with wide desert wheels. Carters are still arguing.

opinions.darby_sumner: Darby works hard and talks harder.
opinions.fenn_tilley: Fenn knows the trade. I will say that for Fenn.

time.night: Lamps are lit. Craft does not end at dusk, only the pay does.

dialogue.aside: You know me. You know my work. I will not insult either by modesty.

greeting: Do not shake my hand. You will be blue until Tuesday.
Buying or looking? Looking is free until you break something.
rumour: A bolt of good blue went missing. The thief is easy to spot: the man not wearing it.
Orders are good and the deadlines are cruel. The festival is early and the work is late.
The Dunhallow Wagon Yard drew a stranger last month. He asked questions and bought nothing.

opinions.elka_stannard: Elka works hard and talks harder.
opinions.seren_yoxall: I would trust Seren with a purse. A small one.

time.rain: Rain on the roof. Good for the colour, bad for the drying.

dialogue.aside: Hello. A pause. I am glad you came. That is all.

greeting: Mind the vat. It looks like water. It is not.
Good tools, good timber, good time. Pick any two.
rumour: The stream ran red on dye day. Children upstream think it is an omen. We let them.
A tool went missing from the bench. Then another. Then the bench.

opinions.gerda_blackmore: Gerda knows the trade. I will say that for Gerda.

time.morning: Morning. The shop is open if you are.

dialogue.aside: You know me. You know my work. I will not insult either by modesty.

greeting: Gloves are by the door. Hands stay blue for days without them.
First time in Dunhallow? The Dunhallow Wagon Yard is the place to start.
rumour: A bolt came out the wrong colour. The wrong colour sold for more. Do not ask me why.
A rival workshop in the next valley pays double for our apprentices. The apprentices are listening.
Ask in Dunhallow who built the Dunhallow Wagon Yard and you will get a different name each time.

opinions.talbot_hornby: Talbot works hard and talks harder.

time.evening: Closing up. Come back tomorrow and bring coin.

dialogue.aside: Welcome, welcome. Your name is right there. On the tip of my tongue.

greeting: Hush. I am counting threads.
You will hear Dunhallow before you see it. Ask at the Dunhallow Wagon Yard.
rumour: Shuttle went missing off the loom. Nobody takes a shuttle. Someone did.
The Dunhallow Wagon Yard has seen odder days than this. Nobody remembers when.

opinions.elka_stannard: Elka knows the trade. I will say that for Elka.
opinions.sorrel_tallis: Sorrel works hard and talks harder.

dialogue.aside: Eh? Oh, it is you. I heard that. I always hear friends.

greeting: Mind the loom. It has a temper, and so do I.
rumour: A shuttle knocked itself off the loom at midnight. No draught. No cat. Just the knock.
When Dunhallow is quiet we say it is peaceful. When it is very quiet we say nothing.

opinions.godric_kettle: Godric works hard and talks harder.
opinions.greta_tallis: Greta and I share a roof and a temper. Mostly the temper.

time.rain: Rain on the roof. Good for the colour, bad for the drying.

dialogue.aside: You know me. You know my work. I will not insult either by modesty.

greeting: Feel that. Go on. That is a week of someone's life.
rumour: Bolts from Silverford come folded wrong. Someone opens them and refolds them. Who has the time?
Dunhallow lives by wheelwrights and carters. When that fails, so do we.

opinions.bartle_bramble: Bartle works hard and talks harder.
opinions.darby_sumner: Darby knows the trade. I will say that for Darby.

time.morning: Morning. The shop is open if you are.

dialogue.aside: Knock on wood, friend. Now touch iron. There. Safe, for a while.

greeting: Hold the mule. He is not as bad as he looks.
rumour: Wolves tracked a cart for two miles last week. I counted the miles, not the wolves.
Every few years Dunhallow has a winter nobody forgets. The old folk say this one is early.

opinions.bartle_bramble: Bartle knows the trade. I will say that for Bartle.
opinions.cressa_brook: Cressa works hard and talks harder.

time.evening: Closing up. Come back tomorrow and bring coin.

greeting: Need a strong back? I have one, a bit used.
rumour: Hands wanted everywhere and nobody pays for hands.
Folk say Dunhallow was founded by someone who wanted to be left alone. We have not forgotten.

opinions.darby_sumner: Darby works hard and talks harder.

time.night: Lamps are lit. Craft does not end at dusk, only the pay does.

dialogue.aside: Take something. Anything. No, a bigger something. I insist.

greeting: Are you a soldier? You look like a soldier.
rumour: The big kids say there is a ghost in the barn. I have not checked. Yet.
Orders are good and the deadlines are cruel. The festival is early and the work is late.

opinions.sorrel_tallis: Sorrel is blood. That settles most arguments and starts the rest.

clues.note: A rag stained with a colour the shop does not mix. The stain is fresh.
The hasp was prised off and set back almost straight. The lock only looks shut.
Someone re-inked a line of the count. The ink is newer than the page.

stashes.say: You lift three bars of rim iron.
You lift three bolts of undyed cloth from the rack.
